We need to use JUnit5, Mockito. Use parameterized tests where appropriate.

We need to create custom Indicator implementations for constant, custom sequences, shifted indicator, throwing indicator, null value indicator.

We need to test NullPointerException when passing null. Also IllegalArgumentException for NaN, mismatched series, null Num.

We need to test rule.isSatisfied behavior.

We need to ensure series used matches expectations.

We have series defined with values; we can create custom Indicator that returns predetermined values based on index.

Implementation: create inner static class SimpleIndicator implements Indicator<Num> with array of Num values and series reference.

ShiftedIndicator: implement Indicator<Num> that returns delegate.getValue(index - shift) or null if out of bounds.

ThrowingIndicator: getValue throws RuntimeException.

NullValueIndicator: getValue returns null.

For mismatched series: create another MockBarSeries.

Test cases group wise.

We'll add @Nested classes for grouping maybe.

Use @ParameterizedTest with MethodSource for multiple cases.

But many cases have unique setups; we can write separate test methods.

Let's outline:

Test null indicator: expect NullPointerException.

Test constant other 5 with numericIndicator also constant 5: numericIndicator must be constant 5. Our numericIndicator currently wraps closePriceIndicator (values from series). Instead we can create numericIndicator = NumericIndicator.of(new ConstantIndicator<>(series, numFunction.apply(5)))? Actually ConstantIndicator constructor takes series and Num value. So we can create constantNumeric = NumericIndicator.of(new ConstantIndicator<>(series, numFunction.apply(5))). Then crossedOver with ConstantIndicator(5) -> rule.isSatisfied(0) false.

Test crossing scenario: numericIndicator values [2,4] and other constant 3. We'll create custom indicator returning 2 at index0, 4 at index1. Use NumericIndicator.of(custom). Then rule.isSatisfied(1) true.

Test numeric values [6,5,4] vs constant 7: rule.isSatisfied(2) false.

Test other same instance: rule.isSatisfied any index false.

Multiple upward crossings: numeric values [3,5,2,6] vs constant 4. Test isSatisfied at 1 true, 2 false, 3 true.

Other decreasing while this constant: numeric constant 5 vs other custom decreasing 6,5,4. rule.isSatisfied(0) false, (2) false.

Other NaN: ConstantIndicator(NaN) -> need Num.NaN; DecimalNum has NaN? There's DecimalNum.NaN? Not sure. Could use DecimalNum.NaN. Use DecimalNum.NaN. Expect IllegalArgumentException when constructing rule? The CrossedUpIndicatorRule constructor may not check NaN; but evaluation may throw. We'll test that rule.isSatisfied(0) throws IllegalArgumentException.

Other same delegate distinct instance: both wrap same ClosePriceIndicator. Should be unsatisfied. Use NumericIndicator.of(closePriceIndicator) for both.

Other shifted indicator: Need ShiftedIndicator that returns null for out-of-range. Use custom.

Mismatched series: create otherSeries = new MockBarSeries(numFunction, ...). Use ConstantIndicator on otherSeries. Expect IllegalArgumentException when constructing rule.

Other throws on getValue: custom indicator that throws. Expect RuntimeException when rule.isSatisfied called.

Other returns null Num: custom indicator getValue returns null. Expect IllegalArgumentException when rule.isSatisfied.

Implement these tests.

Add imports.

Make sure to use assertThrows.

For rule.isSatisfied, CrossedUpIndicatorRule implements Rule with isSatisfied(index). Use rule.isSatisfied(index).

Now produce final test class code.
